stops.name: Quernst
stops.detail: Quernst (approx. 545 m) – northern spur of the Talgang with the ruins of the Quernst Church (at 535 m), the Quernst Chapel and a viewpoint with a view of the Rothaar Mountains and Winterberg.

stops.name: Talgang
stops.detail: In the Eder Heights, on the Talgang mountain in the middle of the forest, lie the ruins of the Quernst Church, which was built around 800 on an old Germanic sanctuary, a sacred grove.

stops.name: Banfebachtal
stops.detail: The last of these waves also reached the Eder Mountains, i.e., today's national park area. There the villages of Eselsbach, located on the Hundsbach in the Gebrannten, Eschenbruch somewhat east of the Fahrentriesch, Wellenhausen in the upper Banfe Valley near the Quernst, Denninghausen in the Bleibach Valley east of the Himbeerkopf, Bodenscheid and Banfe in the lower Banfe Valley, as well as Ermerode on the Elmsberg, were established.

stops.name: Siegelskirche
stops.detail: Another early Christian hilltop church is the Siegelskirche, which was probably also founded on the site of a pre-Christian sacred grove.
